GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2019-10-07T21:51:24Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: ElementReference causes "Invalid JSON" exception when returned to JavaScript
Description: ### Describe the bug
Calling C# from JavaScript, then JavaScript from C# to obtain ElementReferences, then returning those ElementReferences to C#, Blazor throws an exception:
```
blazor.webassembly.js:1 Uncaught (in promise) Error: System.Text.Json.JsonException: Invalid JSON
  at Microsoft.JSInterop.Infrastructure.DotNetDispatcher.EndInvokeJS (/Microsoft.JSInterop.JSRuntime jsRuntime, System.String arguments) <0x20ed888 + 0x000fc> in <4e424253df194e1299a1044d93a79164>:0 
  at Mono.WebAssembly.Interop.MonoWebAssemblyJSRuntime.EndInvokeJS (/System.String argsJson) <0x20e4a58 + 0x0000a> in <d0b620549c284928acbf6b89d371ca02>:0 
    at Object.callMethod (blazor.webassembly.js:1)
    at Object.endInvokeJSFromDotNet (blazor.webassembly.js:1)
    at blazor.webassembly.js:1
```

### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
- .Net Core 3.0.0-100
- dotnet new blazorwasm

Create a JavaScript method that creates an element:
```javascript
window.CreateElement = (text) => {
  var element = document.createElement("span");
  element.innerText = text;
  return element;
}
```
Create a [JSInvokable] C# method:
```csharp
[JSInvokable]
public static async Task<List<ElementReference>> GetElements(){
  List<ElementReference> refs = new List<ElementReference>();
  refs.Add(await JSInterop.InvokeAsync<ElementReference>("CreateElement","first"));
  refs.Add(await JSInterop.InvokeAsync<ElementReference>("CreateElement","second"));
  return refs;
}
```
Create another JavaScript function that calls the C# method:
```javascript
window.Test = async () => {
  var refs = await DotNet.InvokeAsync("TestProject","GetElements");
}
```
Invoke window.Test.

### Expected behavior
Expect no exception to be thrown, and for the elements created by the CreateElement method to be returned to the Test method.
